chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm, from his father, from Ibn Abī Najrān, from ʿĀṣim ibn Ḥumayd, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about one whose hand and foot are amputated. He said: “He washes them both.”

key_terms.الرِّجْلِ: the foot or leg, in the context of the limb mentioned in the ruling
key_terms.الْأَقْطَعِ: a person with an amputated limb
key_terms.الْيَدِ: the hand, in the context of the limb to be washed in wudu (ablution)
key_terms.يَغْسِلُهُمَا: he washes both of them; the legal instruction given in the hadith

ai.seo_question: How does a person with an amputated hand or foot perform wudu (ablution)?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling concerning wudu (ablution) for a person with amputated limbs. It indicates that the remaining parts of the hand and foot are to be washed, showing the application of ritual purity rulings according to one’s physical condition.
